messages:
maria: Heads-up — did a quant bake comparing GPTQ, AWQ, and a small FP8 prototype on the new 13B variant. Ran per-layer variance scans and tried a variance-aware clamp (winsorize-like) plus a tiny per-channel rescale. TL;DR: AWQ +1.2% ppl delta vs FP16 baseline, GPTQ +0.5%, FP8 prototype +3.4% (regression).

jonb: Nice. Which eval sets & metrics? can you paste the high-level numbers?

maria: evals: lm-perplexity on wikitext-like holdout, LlamaEval subset (2k prompts), and our regression promptset (~500 queries). Metrics:
- FP16 baseline: ppl=12.8, rougeL=0.412
- GPTQ (8-bit, channel-wise): ppl=13.0 (+1.6%), rougeL=0.409 (-0.7%)
- AWQ (4/8 hybrid, layerwise ranges): ppl=13.0 (+1.6%), rougeL=0.408 (-0.9%)
- FP8-proto: ppl=13.3 (+3.9%), rougeL=0.400 (-3.0%)
Notes: AWQ and GPTQ similar on aggregate, but errors concentrated in early layers for AWQ.

siva: When you say "concentrated in early layers" do you mean activation std spikes or a few hot channels?

maria: Both. Layer 0-3 show a handful of channels (ch 12, 47, 119) with activation std >> median (x8-x12). Those channels cause tail tokens that the quantization clamps don't capture. I ran a per-channel histogram and the kurtosis is high.

lee: Did you try a selective float fallback for the first N layers? that's usually cheap and helps quality. latency hit?

maria: Yes — fallback float for layers 0-3 (keep FP16) + AWQ for rest: ppl=12.86 (+0.5% vs FP16), rougeL=0.411 (-0.2%). Latency: +4% token latency vs all-AWQ, throughput ~-3% at p99 due to memory bounce on canaries. So cost/latency tradeoff looks good.

oscar: Could we do a "variance-aware clamp" per-channel: compute mean+alpha*std and clamp activation distribution tails before quantization? alpha=3 seemed promising in pilot.

maria: Exactly — I applied winsorize per-channel with alpha=3, then per-channel linear rescale (match pre-quant std). AWQ+winsorize -> ppl=12.95 (+1.0%), rougeL=0.410 (-0.5%). Fewer hallucination failures on the regression set than plain AWQ.

bot-quant: scan-run summary: model=13B-v2, runs=8, script=tools/scan_outliers.py, flagged_layers=[0,1,2,3], flagged_channels={0:[12,47,119],1:[7,88],2:[45],3:[5,90]}, peak-kurtosis=48.2, suggested_action=per-channel-winsorize+fallback-first-4-layers

jonb: Script/command so I can reproduce?

siva: use this: `python tools/scan_outliers.py --model 13B-v2 --quant awq --metric kurtosis --out /tmp/outlier.csv`
Then run winsorize + quant: `python tools/winsorize_and_quant.py --in /models/13B-v2 --out /tmp/13B-awq-winsor --alpha 3.0 --rescale-per-channel`

maria: Quick canary YAML I used:```
routes:
  - name: canary-awq-winsor
    model: 13B-v2
    deploy: awq-winsor
    traffic: 5%
    fallback: float-first-4-layers
    sla: p99_latency_ms<=120
```

lee: Good. Add this to canary and run against production-like traffic replay. Also capture token-level divergence histograms (we care about tail decodes).

oscar: Alternative: instead of winsorize, try per-channel quantile clipping at 99.5th percentile (non-parametric). Might be more robust for heavy tails.

maria: Will try quantile clipping tomorrow. Also plan to test a tiny headwise gating prototype: zero out offending channels during KV cache warmup for first 32 tokens. Very low-cost.

jonb: Add a perf note: AWQ+winsorize increased model binary size by ~6% due to added meta tables. That affects cold start on Private deployments.

maria: Noted — will add an opt to strip per-channel rescale tables for private builds (trades quality).

siva: Can we get a short runbook for when we see these spikes in new models? e.g., detect kurtosis>10 on early layers -> auto-run winsorize + run small regression set -> if delta<1% promote.

maria: Yup — I'll draft a runbook and add it to the evaluation pipeline. Plan: automated scan in onboarding pipeline -> if flagged, run two mitigation presets (winsorize alpha=3 & fallback-first-4-layers) -> pick best by ppl+regression set -> create canary.

lee: :thumbsup: Please attach the raw outlier CSVs and the regression prompts. I'll start a traffic replay.

maria: uploading /tmp/outlier.csv and reg_prompts_v2.json to the onboarding bucket now. I'll post links in the morning.

jonb: Thanks — meeting 10am tomorrow to decide whether to roll AWQ-winsor to dedicated canaries.

maria: sounds good. I'll upload artifacts and the canary config before the meeting.

oscar: If you want, I can prototype the quantile clipper tonight and push results to the thread.

maria: please do, much appreciated.

bot-quant: automation: scheduled job "onboard-scan-13B-v2" will run at 03:00 UTC and post results here.
